adas-equilibrium-s1.title: Output and unemployment in three countries

table.caption: Real GDP, full-employment real GDP and unemployment in three invented countries this year (invented data for practice)

adas-equilibrium-s2.title: The AD-AS graph for Country D

items.q: Based on the table, which country has a recessionary gap?
options: Alta
Bora
Cresh
Alta and Cresh

why.correct: A recessionary gap means real GDP is below full-employment output, with unemployment above the natural rate: Alta.
options: Right: Alta's real GDP (940) is below full-employment output (1,000), and its unemployment is above the natural rate.
Bora produces exactly its full-employment output: it is in long-run equilibrium.
Cresh produces more than full-employment output, an inflationary gap.
Cresh's output is above full employment, which is the opposite kind of gap.

items.q: Using the table, calculate the size of Alta's output gap, in billions of dollars (as a positive number).

why.correct: Gap $=$ full-employment real GDP $-$ real GDP $= 1{,}000 - 940 = 60$ billion dollars, a recessionary gap.

mistakes.why: That is the gap as a percent of full-employment output. The question asks for billions of dollars: $1{,}000 - 940$.
That is the gap in unemployment rates. The output gap is measured in real GDP: $1{,}000 - 940$.

items.q: Based on the table, how does Cresh's short-run equilibrium compare with its LRAS?
options: It lies on LRAS, because the economy is growing
It lies to the right of LRAS, with unemployment below the natural rate
It lies to the left of LRAS, with unemployment above the natural rate
It lies to the right of LRAS, with unemployment above the natural rate

why.correct: Cresh produces above full employment: its AD and SRAS cross to the right of LRAS, and unemployment (3.5%) is below the natural rate (5%).
options: On LRAS, output would equal 1,000. Cresh produces 1,060.
Right: output of 1,060 exceeds full-employment output, an inflationary gap.
That describes Alta, not Cresh.
When output is above potential, firms hire more, so unemployment is below the natural rate.

items.q: Based on the table, which country is in long-run equilibrium?
options: Alta, because unemployment is high enough to keep prices from rising
Cresh, because it produces the most real GDP of the three
Bora, because AD and SRAS cross on LRAS at full-employment output
No country, because each one has some unemployment

why.correct: Long-run equilibrium: AD, SRAS and LRAS meet at one point, with output at full employment. Bora fits.
options: High unemployment means output is below potential, so Alta is not in long-run equilibrium.
Producing above potential is an inflationary gap, not long-run equilibrium.
Right: output equals full-employment output and unemployment equals the natural rate.
Full employment allows natural unemployment. Bora's 5% is its natural rate.

items.q: According to the graph, what kind of gap does Country D have?
options: An inflationary gap, because AD and SRAS cross to the left of LRAS
No gap, because AD and SRAS cross each other
No gap, because LRAS passes through the AD curve
A recessionary gap, because AD and SRAS cross to the left of LRAS

why.correct: In the graph, AD meets SRAS at an output to the left of LRAS: real GDP is below potential, a recessionary gap.
options: Left of LRAS means output below potential, which is a recessionary gap.
They cross, which sets short-run output, but not on LRAS, so there is a gap.
LRAS crosses AD on any such graph; what matters is whether AD and SRAS meet on LRAS. Here they meet to its left.
Right: short-run output is below full-employment output.

items.q: According to the graph, how does Country D's unemployment rate compare with its natural rate?
options: It is above the natural rate, because output is below full employment
It is below the natural rate, because output is below full employment
It equals the natural rate, because SRAS crosses AD
There is no way to compare them, as unemployment is not on the graph

why.correct: Output below full employment means unemployment above the natural rate: there is cyclical unemployment.
options: Right: producing less than potential needs fewer workers, so cyclical unemployment is positive.
Lower output means fewer jobs, so unemployment is above, not below, the natural rate.
Unemployment equals the natural rate only at full-employment output, on LRAS.
Output tells you: below YF, unemployment is above the natural rate.

items.q: Which statement about Country D's position in the graph is correct?
options: It is a long-run equilibrium, because AD equals SRAS
It is a short-run equilibrium but not a long-run equilibrium
It is not an equilibrium, because firms want to produce more
It is both a short-run and a long-run equilibrium

why.correct: Where AD meets SRAS is a short-run equilibrium. It is also a long-run equilibrium only if that point is on LRAS.
options: A long-run equilibrium also needs output on LRAS, at full employment.
Right: planned spending equals output supplied at SRAS, but output is off LRAS.
At the AD-SRAS crossing, the output firms supply equals what buyers plan to buy.
Output is below YF, so it is not on LRAS.

items.q: Label the axes and the three curves of this AD-AS graph.

why.correct: Vertical axis: Price level. Horizontal axis: Real GDP. AD slopes down, SRAS slopes up, LRAS is vertical at full-employment output.

items.q: The economy starts in long-run equilibrium. Households and firms grow pessimistic and cut their spending. Shift the right curve and mark the new short-run equilibrium.

why.correct: Less spending shifts AD left. The new short-run equilibrium is left of LRAS, with a lower price level and lower real GDP: a recessionary gap.

key.because: a fall in consumer and business spending

slips.SRAS: Pessimism cuts spending, which is aggregate demand. Production costs did not change, so SRAS stays put.

items.q: This economy is in an inflationary gap. Mark a point X on the AD curve that would be a long-run equilibrium at the same LRAS.

why.correct: Long-run equilibrium is on LRAS. Moving along AD to full-employment output means less output and a higher price level than now.

items.q: What defines short-run equilibrium in the AD-AS model?
options: The price level and real GDP where AD crosses LRAS
Real GDP at full employment
The price level and real GDP where AD crosses SRAS
The price level at which unemployment is zero

why.correct: Short-run equilibrium: where AD meets SRAS. Long-run equilibrium: where AD, SRAS and LRAS all meet.
options: AD crossing LRAS gives the long-run outcome only when SRAS passes through the same point.
That is where LRAS stands. Short-run output can differ from it.
Right: there, planned spending equals the output firms supply.
Even at full employment there is natural unemployment; equilibrium is where AD meets SRAS.

items.q: An economy's AD and SRAS cross at a real GDP of 1,200 billion dollars, and LRAS is at 1,150 billion dollars. Which describes the economy?
options: A recessionary gap of 50 billion dollars, with unemployment above the natural rate
An inflationary gap of 50 billion dollars, with unemployment above the natural rate
Long-run equilibrium, because AD and SRAS cross
An inflationary gap of 50 billion dollars, with unemployment below the natural rate

why.correct: Real GDP 1,200 > full-employment 1,150: an inflationary (positive) gap of 50 billion dollars, unemployment below the natural rate.
options: Output is above potential, not below it.
Above-potential output needs more workers, so unemployment is below the natural rate.
The crossing is 50 billion to the right of LRAS, so the economy is not at long-run equilibrium.
Right: output exceeds potential by 50 billion, so firms are hiring beyond full employment.

items.q: An economy is in long-run equilibrium. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: AD, SRAS and LRAS cross at one point
Unemployment equals the natural rate
Unemployment is zero
Real GDP is above full-employment output
The price level has stopped changing for good

why.correct: In long-run equilibrium, AD meets SRAS on LRAS: output is at full employment and unemployment equals the natural rate.
options: Right: that is what long-run equilibrium means on the graph.
Right: output is at full employment, so there is no cyclical unemployment.
Frictional and structural unemployment remain at full employment.
In long-run equilibrium real GDP equals full-employment output.
A long-run equilibrium can shift when AD or supply changes; it is a resting point, not a permanent one.

items.q: Full-employment real GDP is 2,000 billion dollars and actual real GDP is 1,900 billion dollars. Calculate the recessionary gap as a percent of full-employment output.

mistakes.why: 100 is the gap in billions of dollars. As a percent, divide it by full-employment output and multiply by 100.
You divided by actual output. The gap is measured against full-employment output, 2,000.

items.q: Make it specific: describe an economy whose AD and SRAS cross to the left of LRAS.

why.correct: Output is below full employment, a recessionary gap, so unemployment is above the natural rate.

specific.frame: Real GDP is ___ full-employment output, which is a ___ gap, so unemployment is ___ the natural rate.
specific.model: Real GDP is below full-employment output, which is a recessionary gap, so unemployment is higher than the natural rate because firms need fewer workers.

output.label: Real GDP
options: below
above

why.1: Left of LRAS on the horizontal axis means less output.

gap.label: The gap
options: recessionary
inflationary

why.1: An inflationary gap has output above full employment.

unemployment.label: Unemployment
options: above
below

why.1: Lower output needs fewer workers, so unemployment is higher.

items.q: On an AD-AS graph, the short-run equilibrium is at PL1 and Y1, and Y1 is to the right of LRAS. Where should YF be labeled?
options: On the horizontal axis where LRAS stands, to the left of Y1
On the horizontal axis at Y1
On the vertical axis at PL1
On the horizontal axis to the right of Y1

why.correct: Label YF where LRAS meets the real GDP axis; with Y1 to its right, the gap between them is the inflationary gap.
options: Right: YF is full-employment output, where the vertical LRAS meets the real GDP axis.
Y1 is actual output. In an inflationary gap it is to the right of YF.
YF is an output level, so it goes on the real GDP axis.
Y1 is right of LRAS, so YF lies to the left of Y1.
